name: pcb-p-pack
title: PCB-P PACK BMS

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._stitch_prune_why: 12 September 2026, P3, and it is A24's case on a two-layer board. P routed 0 hard and 0 unrouted and check_pcb_p refused it for ONE item of 143: a locked GND via at (93.6, 101.3) whose B.Cu end sits outside the ground fill, because the router ran /PACK_F 0.76 mm past it and the fill retreated by its clearance. Two tracks land on the via and both are on F.Cu, so its B.Cu end connects to nothing. Measured on a copy of the routed board before this was turned on: 1 locked via removed of 124, 0 left alone, hard 0 and unrouted 0 both unchanged, and the gate's one failure gone. It stays judged against the board before it (finish.sh 5b) and reverts if it opens anything. NOT the same via as the one that started this: U1's exposed pad had a single thermal via because escape.py was refusing the other four against the land's own solder-paste apertures, and with that fixed all five of its vias reach the B.Cu fill (appendix 32.151).
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.
finish._stub_layers_why: 15 September 2026 (P5): the back side is the ground plane and the pack bands; a closure on B.Cu would cut the pour under a front-side signal, which is the gap rule 1 refuses. The stub router closes on F.Cu only.
finish._via_parallel_why: 18 September 2026 (rule PI-003): after every copper-editing stage and before the ground vias, via_parallel lays parallel barrels beside any via dc_drop's solved mesh puts over IPC-2221's rating for its wall (the fabricator's 18 um plating), joined on every layer the net touches there, DRC-guarded, then re-solves and re-judges. On the committed board: P4 passes PI-003; the stage lays nothing and says so

_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026, THE DECLARATION IS THE BOARD IN THIS TREE AND NOT THE ROUTE IN FLIGHT. It was set to the in-flight phase on 16 September with the reason that final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared one, and that is exactly what went wrong: every reader that GATES on this field asks 'is this folder the board', so pointing it at a route that has not landed makes those gates answer about a board that does not exist. Board P proved the cost: its P4 folder holds the board this tree holds, byte for byte (sha256 d79865e7b1aceb95), and it was being read as stale against a declared P5 that was measured, refused and abandoned under decision 28. Board A declared A36, a route that was never cut, while the tree carries A32. The phase in flight belongs to the RUN (`routeflow --phase`, with ROUTEFLOW_PHASE_UNDECLARED=1 for an arm whose board may never be adopted), and it moves into this field in the same commit that brings the board in.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

signal_classes.basis: SMBus at 100 kHz, open drain, the edge set by the pull-up and the bus capacitance
the gauge's battery-trip interrupt, an edge into the host
the pack-present pin, a static level pulled through a resistor
the display-request button input, pressed by a person
the push-button input of the gauge, the same
a thermistor divider, a DC level changing with temperature
a cell-voltage sense line through its filter, DC by construction
a cell tap, a DC node of the pack
a shunt sense line through its filter, millivolts of DC
the charge FET gate drive and its return, switched at most once per charge cycle
the discharge FET gate drive and its return, the same
the gauge's own supply after its filter
the protector's switched node between the two FETs, a DC node except at a protection event
the battery sense node through its filter

_gnd_grid_why: MEASURED AND REJECTED for this board, 15 September 2026 (/root/piso4 against /root/piso4g). Four-layer P without the grid routes 0 hard and 0 unrouted of 35 nets in 1.4 minutes; with a 2.1 mm ground-via grid laid before the route the same board ends its rounds at 3 and then 21 unrouted. P is 70 by 44 mm carrying the pack path in wide bands, so a grid of stitch vias takes the room the router needs, and prevention that costs the route is not prevention. The return-via fixer works on P after the route instead. This is a declaration of what was tried, not an omission: a board that declares nothing gets no grid and nobody can tell why.
_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED. Board P is ordered at 2 oz by owner ruling 7, and the fabricator's capability page states its annular ring rows for 1 oz only (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md, read 16 September 2026). Borrowing the 1 oz number for a 2 oz board would be inventing a limit, and etching a heavier copper takes MORE room rather than less, so the 1 oz figure is not even conservative here. The ring stays unjudged on this board until the fabricator is asked directly, which is a question for the order.
_copper_layers_why: Two layers as built. OWNER DECISION 28 IS OPEN on this: two layers cannot hold the return-path rule and the four-layer arm routes 0 and 0 in 1.4 minutes. If the ruling goes to four, this is the line that changes.
_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. NOTHING ON BOARD P LEAVES THE ENCLOSURE, and this is the sentence that says so rather than a file nobody wrote. P is the pack's own protection and gauge board and it sits in the case beside the cells: J_CELL is the 4S tap harness to the cell block a few centimetres away, J_TS is the thermistor lead into that same block, J_SMB is the gauge's bus to board E inside the case, and the pack current leaves on W_BP and W_BN, two soldered wire lands to board E's own entry. Every one of those conductors begins and ends inside the sealed case, so the electrostatic and surge argument that TRN-001 is about does not reach them: what reaches them is board E's inlet protection, upstream, which decision 31 covers. If a pack lead is ever brought out to a case connector this declaration is the first thing that has to change.

GND.what: the board's single ground: every return on this board is this net

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k
_safety_lines_why: The pack board carries no line whose assertion inhibits a hazard: its protection is the pack's own protector and the blade fuse, both of which act without a signal, and nothing on it is inhibited by a conductor from anywhere else.
_class_table_why: 18 September 2026 10:55 CEST: gen_pcb_p3.py wrote a hand-typed class table into the project file with SENSE at 0.6/0.3 (a 0.15 mm ring) where the API said 0.7/0.3 since the E12 annular finding, and the project file is what the router reads; P4 predates both. One CLASSES table feeds both now.
_p7_route_why: P7 (18 September 2026 10:59 UTC, /root/prf7, $SP/p7.sh): board P re-cut at the CORRECTED design rules. The committed P4 is drawn to 0.127 mm track and clearance where the fabricator's own rows read 0.16 for 2 oz on two layers, which is why STK-001 and RTE-001 read FAIL on this board today: `fab_limits` judges the RULES and the generator was corrected on 16 September while no P board was ever cut on it (the P6 arm of that night has no recorded result). P7 also carries the one class table of 18 September (the project file now says SENSE 0.7/0.3 where P4's said 0.6/0.3 and named no SENSE class at all), the thermal vias in every exposed pad and today's judging path. P4 routed 0 hard and 0 unrouted, so this is a re-cut and not an experiment; if it lands 0/0 it clears two of board P's five failures, and its folder still waits on decision 28 (two layers against four) and the paperwork. RESULT (11:21 UTC): 0 hard, 47 unrouted of 35 nets, 12 vias, 21.9 minutes of autoroute. That is the THIRD independent reading that two-layer P at the fabricator's own 0.16 mm floor does not route (P6 43, the 15 September arm 45, P7 47) against four-layer P's 0 and 0, and it settles what P4's 0/0 was worth: it was routed at 0.127 mm track and clearance, which the fabricator does not build at 2 oz on two layers. The table leaves no third way, because 0.10/0.10 needs 1 oz and ruling 7 refused 1 oz for this board on its own current density. Decision 28 now has three numbers instead of one. P7 is NOT adopted: a board with 47 open connections is not a candidate, and the phase declaration stays at P4 until the layer count is ruled.
_p8_route_why: P8 (18 September 2026 11:25 UTC, /root/prf8, $SP/p8_4l.sh): decision 28's OPTION 1 measured at rules the fabricator builds. Four layers, In1 and In2 as ground planes, wires on F.Cu and B.Cu, via minimums 0.45/0.25, and today's 0.16 mm floor, which is legal on both stacks (2 oz two-layer is 0.16/0.16 and 2 oz multilayer 0.15/0.15). WHY IT IS NEEDED: the four-layer arm of 15 September routed 0 hard and 0 unrouted, and it was routed at 0.127 mm track and clearance, which is exactly the defect that makes P4's own 0/0 worthless. The recommendation in decision 28 therefore rested on a number taken at rules the fabricator does not build for this copper weight on either stack. Nothing here is committed: the layer count is a reserved class and this is the measurement the ruling needs beside P7's 47 open on two layers. RESULT (11:31 UTC, six minutes of routing): **0 hard, 0 unrouted of 35 nets, 98 vias**, the profile's prediction MET. So decision 28 now has both of its numbers taken at rules the fabricator actually builds: two layers at 2 oz leave 43, 45 and 47 open across three runs, four layers at 2 oz close the board in six minutes. Its finish runs; the board is NOT adopted and the phase declaration stays P4, because the layer count is a reserved class and this is the owner's ruling to make. ITS GATES, read on that board: routed-board gate PASS (hard 0, unrouted 0), check_pcb_p PASS 51 of 51, via_audit PASS of 279 with no via under either floor, class_floor PASS, dc_drop PASS 3 of 3 rails (one density note), impedance PASS (this board declares no pair target), and fab_limits PASS of 20. ONE CAVEAT FOR THE RULING: the four-layer stackup this arm generated is the 1 oz one, and ruling 7 orders board P at 2 oz. At 2 oz multilayer the fabricator's floor is 0.15 mm, which this board's 0.16 still clears, so the copper decision does not change the routing answer; what it changes is the stackup the board file declares and the current density dc_drop judges against, both of which are a line in the generator rather than a route. The finish itself stopped at CONTRACTS NOT JUDGED because boards A and E had just been regenerated on the runner and their netlists in that tree named an older engine; that is a staging artefact, not a property of this board, and both netlists are regenerated and committed now.
_stackup_dk_why: STK-001 RESIDUE, OWED TO THIS BOARD'S NEXT GENERATION (18 September 2026, stackup_gate's first run). The board file carries epsilon_r 4.6 on its FR-4 core where the named record for the 2L-2oz stack says 4.5. The record is right: the fabricator's own capability document states the dielectric constant per build and gives 4.5 for a two-layer board (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md), while the 4.6 in this board file came from its impedance page, which is about the multilayer cores, and was corrected in stackup_write.py on 16 September. Nothing computed on this board moves: it carries no impedance target, so the number reaches no verdict except this one. It is NOT patched into the committed board file, because rewriting a board changes its sha and stales every reading taken on it for a number that changes nothing; the next generation writes the stack from stackup_write.STACKS and carries 4.5 by construction. Until then STK-001 reads FAIL of 8 on this board and says exactly this.
_pi003_sites_why: BOARD P HAS FOUR BARRELS OVER THEIR OWN WALL, measured 18 September 2026 on the committed P4 with barrel_sites.py while the same rule was being answered on boards D and E. All four are 0.50 mm barrels rated 1.051 A at a 10 K rise on the fabricator's plating: FUSED 1.485 A (ratio 1.41) at case (-7.23, 16.1) and 1.742 A (1.66) at (-3.15, 14.36), PACK_P 1.965 A (1.87) at (14.78, 14.06), and one more. This is the pack current crossing layers on a two-layer board, and it is the same shape as board D's and board E's: a transition the generator gave one barrel. The corridors are workable: the worst FUSED site has Q1's three source pads of its own net at 0.68 to 2.63 mm with Q1 pad 4 (CHG_G) the nearest obstacle at 1.43 mm, and PACK_P's has Q2's three pads at 4.31 to 4.58 mm. **Nothing is drawn**, because decision 28 decides whether board P is two layers or four and a four-layer P is regenerated from its own floor plan; whichever way it goes, `power_copper.stitch(..., amps=)` now refuses a stitch that is short of barrels, so the next P carries the check even if nobody remembers this note. Board C was measured the same way and has NONE. AND MORE BARRELS IS NOT BOARD P'S ANSWER, which its own generator comment already half says (read 18 September 2026 16:50 UTC). All four over-rated barrels are LOCKED, so they are the generator's own, and they are already the product of a campaign: each of the three source tracks per FET carries TWO vias at 3.15 and 4.05 mm from the pad, 0.9 mm apart, six per FET where there were three, and the record of that campaign says why the earlier attempts failed, 'five attempts at the band's own stations moved the worst barrel from 2.67 A to 1.88 because they were all downstream of this point'. The four that are still over sit AT the FET's source pads, which is where the current enters, and the tracks are 1.93 mm long so there is no room for a third via along them; a wider hole does not close it either (0.6 mm is the most the 0.9 mm pitch allows at this project's 0.2995 hole-to-hole floor, and it carries 1.26 A against PACK_P's 1.965). So what is left is geometry rather than count: vias IN the FET's source pads, or a path that does not change layer at the pad at all. Both are design choices for the next P generation and both interact with decision 28, which decides whether this board is two layers or four. Nothing is drawn.
_ret002_p_why: RET-002 ON BOARD P IS TWO LAYERS (18 September 2026, re-taken read-only on P4). Five nets of 29 are over their limit and the separation of another conductor's via anti-pads changed NOTHING on this board, which is what a two-layer board should read: there is no inner plane to punch a hole in, so an uncovered run is a run with nothing under it. `SMBC` is 102.3 mm of 123.0 without a reference against a 30.0 mm limit, `SMBC_I` 42.4 of 47.8, `PACK_F` 33.1 of 34.5 and `FUSE` 11.1 of 17.6. Board P is the control that says today's change to the screen is not a loosening, and its own reading is owner decision 28's question (two layers against four) rather than a routing one.
_rail_crossings_why: BOARD P'S PRE-ROUTE BARREL READING IS ZERO OF FIVE (19 September 2026, `rail_crossings.py` on the committed P4, read-only). Not one of board P's declared crossings carries the barrels its current needs, and the worst is the pack lead itself: **`CELL4` at W_BP pad 1 (73.00, 87.50) crosses on ONE 0.50 mm barrel carrying 18.00 A, where the same arithmetic asks for EIGHTEEN.** The others: `CELL4` at F1 pad 1, 5.00 A of its 10.00 over two pads through one barrel, needs five; `FUSED` at Q1 pads 2 and 3, 3.33 A each of 10.00 over three pads, needs four apiece. It is the conservative bound, because the solved mesh spreads what a pad's copper actually carries and `via_current` on the same board names four sites rather than five; the shape is the same and the answer is the generator's, points added to the calls that place those vias. It rides with whatever P phase decision 28 produces, because board P's layer count is the reserved question and no P board is being cut until it is ruled.
_rail_barrels_why: BOARD P HAS FIVE CROSSINGS TO ANSWER AND TWO THE ARITHMETIC OVERSTATES (19 September 2026, `rail_barrels.py` on a placement regenerated at P4 with today's tools, board and intent written the same minute): 9 crossings judged, SEVEN short. Five are answerable beside the pad and they AGREE with the solved reading that made decision 28's residue: `CELL4` at F1 pad 1 (5.00 A, one 0.50 mm barrel, needs five), `FUSED` at Q1 pads 1 and 3 and `PACK_P` at Q2 pads 1 and 3 (3.33 A apiece over three barrels, one more each). **THE OTHER TWO ARE THE LIMIT OF THE PRE-ROUTE QUESTION AND ARE WORTH WRITING DOWN AS SUCH.** `CELL4` at W_BP pad 1 and `PACK_P` at W_P pad 1 are the 12 AWG SOLDER WIRE LANDS, and the tool asks them for 18 and 25 barrels because it attributes the WHOLE declared rail current to a crossing at the source pad. Board P is two layers at 2 oz and its pack current largely does not cross: `via_current` on P's ROUTED board reads FUSED at 1.66 and PACK_P at 1.87 times their rating, not eighteen amps through one barrel. So the pre-route reading is an UPPER BOUND at a source pad, the cap correctly refuses to draw a busbar there, and the solved mesh is what decides those two. Read a declined site as a question, not as a finding.
_stk001_residue_why: STK-001 IS ONE LINE AND IT CANNOT BE APPLIED ALONE (19 September 2026, verified rather than assumed). The board carries `epsilon_r 4.6` in its stackup block where the 2-layer 2 oz record says **4.5**, from the fabricator's own capability page, and that is the whole disagreement: `stackup_write.py` rewritten over a copy of this board changes **exactly one line** and nothing else, and the tool is pure text with no KiCad behind it, so the edit costs a second. **What it cannot do is stand alone.** This board's deliverable folder holds it BYTE FOR BYTE (sha256 identical on both sides), which is what DFM-001 and DOC-001 read; changing the board without re-cutting the folder breaks a rule that passes today to fix one that fails, and re-cutting the folder is blocked behind decision 31 for the boards that hold the set. So the deferral of 18 September stands and now carries its reason: **the fix is a line, the obstacle is the folder**, and STK-001 closes itself in the same commit that re-cuts this board's deliverable. The number changes nothing electrically on a board with no impedance target; it is the record being true about what was built.
_board_p_state_why: 19 September 2026 10:05 CEST, BOARD P'S FIVE FAILURES, AND THREE OF THEM ARE ONE RULING (33 of 47 verified). STK-001, RET-002 and RTE-001 are all decision 28 and all three say the same thing in different instruments: the committed P4 is drawn to 0.127 mm track and clearance where the fabricator's rows read 0.16 for 2 oz on two layers, P7 re-cut at that floor routes 47 open (the third independent reading after 43 and 45), and P8 at four layers closes 0 hard and 0 unrouted in six minutes with check_pcb_p 51 of 51. BAT-001 is decision 40, the pack's cell-level protection being one firmware-configured device. OUT-001 is the set's. So board P has NO engineering item at all: every failure it carries is one of two rulings, and the measurements both rulings need are taken and in the record. Counts are generated in v2/docs/PCB-OPEN-PAIRS.md; this paragraph is what that page cannot know.
_p_switch_list_measured: BOARD P'S SWITCHING LIST HAD ONE CANDIDATE IT NEVER MENTIONED, AND MEASURING IT COST THE READING NOTHING (19 September 2026, switch_list.py on board P's committed netlist, then sensitive_nodes read-only on its own frozen board). ANA-001 measures a sensitive node's clearance from the nearest SWITCHING copper and which copper is switching is a DECLARATION, so an undeclared switching net is copper the reading never looks at. Board P declares `switch_nets: []` with the reason that the board is linear and its only edges are the SMBus and the FET gate drive. That sentence does not mention `/SW`, and `/SW` carries **Q1 pin 5 and Q2 pin 5**, the common DRAIN of the pack's back-to-back protection pair, which is switching shaped by the report's own predicate. It is ranked WEAK (no inductor on it), and the report is deliberately a REPORT because whether a protection pair's common drain is switching copper for this rule is a judgement: it moves at a protection event and at a charge or discharge enable, never at a converter's switching frequency. **THE JUDGEMENT DID NOT HAVE TO BE MADE, BECAUSE IT WAS MEASURED.** With `/SW` declared as switching in a THROWAWAY copy of the declaration, on board P's own frozen board (sha d79865e7b1aceb95, identical before and after), all seven nodes are measured and **all seven PASS**: `SRN_F` 1.717 mm, `VC2_F` 2.487, `VC1_F` 5.332, `VC3_F` 8.094, `TS1` 9.575, `SRP_F` 10.091, `VC4_F` 10.130, against the 0.50 mm each asks. The worst is 3.4 times the floor. So board P reads PASS of 7 whether `/SW` is in the list or not, the exclusion is free, and `pcb_sensitive.yaml` now NAMES it with that number rather than being silent about it. The same question asked of the other boards: **board A 17 switching-shaped nets and ZERO undeclared** of 23 declared, so A49's ANA-001 answer will be read against a complete denominator; **board D zero shaped** beside a declared empty list; board E zero undeclared (measured 19 September). Board P was the only one with a gap and it is a gap in the WORDS, not in the copper.
_dc_conductors_declared_as_nodes: A DC CONDUCTOR DECLARED AS A NODE IS JUDGED BY NEITHER POWER RULE (20 September 2026, 00:25 CEST; the set-wide count is in the appendix addendum of that time). `intent.node()` describes, in its own words, a net that is NOT a rail, and it exists for CMP-001, which asks what voltage a part on a net can see. `dc_drop` solves RAILS. So every net on this board that carries a load's DC current and got a node instead of a rail is copper PI-001 and PI-002 have never looked at. The one instance measured so far, board A's CH_ACN, read 476 mV of drop and 4.81 A in a 0.500 mm inner conductor rated 0.40 A. ON THIS BOARD IT IS ONE NET AND IT IS THE BIGGEST CURRENT IN THE KIT: `PACK_N`, the pack negative, one 2 mOhm shunt from ground, carrying the pack's whole 10.0 A typical and 18.0 A peak. Three rails are judged on this board and the return is not one of them. It is the first of the sixteen to do, with board A's CH_SRP. Each needs its source, its loads and its budget written down before it is declared, because a wrong declaration is worse than a missing one: it produces a number.
